claims.text: The as-synthesized equimolar nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has a homogeneous elemental distribution.
A moderate oxidative pretreatment at 0.4–0.7 V vs. RHE induces surface segregation in equimolar nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs.
The pretreatment enriches Pt at the catalyst surface.
The pretreatment enriches Pd at the catalyst surface.
The oxidative pretreatment drives selective rearrangement of surface atoms.
Pretreatment-induced surface rearrangement alters the local electronic environment.
The altered local electronic environment lowers the energy barrier for C–C bond cleavage in adsorbed ethanol intermediates.
Lowering the barrier for C–C bond cleavage favors complete ethanol oxidation to CO2.
Pt/Pd surface enrichment enhances ethanol-oxidation selectivity toward CO2 over partial oxidation products.
Relative to an untreated catalyst, the pretreated catalyst will produce a higher relative yield of CO2 under identical reaction conditions.
Relative to an untreated catalyst, the pretreated catalyst will produce less acetaldehyde and other partial oxidation products.
Potentials of approximately 0.4–0.7 V vs. RHE are conducive to surface restructuring of this catalyst during ethanol oxidation.
The predicted segregation and selectivity change are expected to hold in acidic aqueous electrolyte at approximately 0.4–0.7 V vs. RHE.
Departures from the specified electrolyte or potential range may prevent the predicted surface segregation or selectivity change.
Prior observations support effects of surface segregation on catalytic behavior.
